title: UEFA Champions League
summary:
This document is a comprehensive overview of the UEFA Champions League (UCL), the annual European club football competition organized by UEFA. The article begins with an introduction describing the competition's prestige, noting it is the most-watched club competition in the world, tracing its evolution from the European Champion Clubs' Cup (founded 1955) to its current name (adopted 1992), and summarizing its current format, dominance statistics by nation (led by Spain with 20 wins), and notable achievements such as Real Madrid's record 15 titles.

The **History** section traces the competition's precursors (the 1895 World Championship, Challenge Cup, Mitropa Cup, Coupe des Nations, and Latin Cup), the founding inspired by Gabriel Hanot of L'Équipe, and chronicles the tournament's evolution through distinct eras: Real Madrid's dominance in the early years (1955–1967), Dutch and West German club supremacy (1968–1976) led by Ajax and Bayern Munich, English dominance followed by the Heysel Stadium disaster and the rebranding into the Champions League (1977–1997), and finally Spanish and English club dominance with league expansion (1998–present).

Additional sections cover:
- **Anthem**: The competition's musical identity composed by Tony Britten, adapted from Handel's Zadok the Priest, and its performances at finals
- **Branding**: The creation of the "starball" logo and consistent visual identity by TEAM
- **Format**: Detailed explanations of the qualification system (including UEFA coefficients, qualifying streams, and title holder rules), the new 36-team Swiss-style league phase introduced in 2024–25, the knockout phase structure, and the access list distribution
- **Prizes**: The European Champion Clubs' Cup trophy details, medal allocations, and the breakdown of prize money by stage
- **Sponsorship**: The multi-sponsor corporate model, LED and virtual advertising technology, and jersey sponsorship regulations
- **Media coverage**: Television audience figures highlighting the final as the most-watched annual sporting event
- **Records and statistics**: Performances by club and nation, player records for wins, appearances, goals, and assists
- **Awards**: The Player of the Season and Young Player of the Season awards introduced in 2021–22

The article concludes with links to continental equivalents such as the AFC Champions League Elite, CAF Champions League, CONCACAF Champions Cup, and Copa Libertadores.
